newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine foreign minister to meet Britain's Cook.
newsitem.headline: Argentine foreign minister to meet Britain's Cook.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella has scheduled a meeting with his new British counterpart, Robin Cook, next month, a Foreign Ministry official said on Friday.
During the June 13 meeting, Di Tella will raise the issue of a possible visit by President Carlos Menem to Britain, the official said in an interview.

A Menem trip would be the first by an Argentine president since the two nations went to war in 1982 after a military junta tried to enforce Argentina's claim on the disputed Falkland islands by sending in troops. About 1,000 servicemen died in the 10-week clash.

Menem's government has raised hopes for its claim to sovereignty of the British-run islands since Britain's Labour Party swept into power after May 1 general elections, ending 18 years of Conservative rule.

A week ago Di Tella said: "You think I have lost my mind. Nevertheless, I say it is now conceivable, we are now seeing signs that this could reach a final solution before Menem's mandate ends" in 1999.

After Labour won the election Menem repeated his vow that "Argentina's flags will fly on the islands by the year 2000," but made clear there would be no repeat of the war over the islands Argentina calls Malvinas.
